text:
Aisha Patel: Quick heads-up — account showing a sharp activity dip: 45% fewer active seats over the last 14d and average daily calls to the API down 60%. New procurement contact (we got a note from their side) and there’s rumour of a competitive PoC. Marking as renewal-risk triage.

Tom Nguyen: Yikes. Can you drop the dashboard link + top 5 users? Need to see whether this is core-product drop or a single team.

Aisha Patel: Dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.example/acme-retail/usage — last 14d filter. Payload I pulled: 
```sql
select team, count(distinct user_id) as active_users, sum(api_calls) as calls_last_14d
from usage_events
where account_id = 'acme-retail' and event_ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
group by team
order by calls_last_14d desc
```
Top teams: "Catalog" (down 70%), "Customer-Support" (steady), "Integrations" (down 55%).

Lina Morales: Thanks. Do we know if they switched to on-prem or toggled rate limits? Any infra/latency alerts from eng-runtime?

Ravi Shah: eng-runtime reports no errors or latency spikes for their model routes. Seen a few 403s from a new IP block last week — looks like a procurement-driven key rotation. engage-bot posted the key-change event.

engage-bot: Key rotation detected for account acme-retail by user:marta.procurement@acme (2026-03-12T09:22Z) — API keys revoked: 2, created: 1

Tom Nguyen: Procurement-led key rotation + Catalog team drop = classic procurement/contract pause pattern. Could be they paused the Catalog integration during negotiation.

Jen Ortiz: I’ll reach out to the CSM sponsor (Victor) to confirm if this is a tactical pause or evaluation. If it’s evaluation, we should request the PoC scope and timeline so we can propose an interim fallback (lower-cost model variant + batching) to keep core workflows alive.

Aisha Patel: Good plan. Can someone prepare a short cost/latency fallback options doc for Victor by EOD? He cares about seat cost and SLA.

Lina Morales: I can draft two options: 1) thin-client fallback (smaller model, aggressive batching) — saves ~40% token cost; 2) hybrid edge-caching (prefix cache for catalog queries) — saves latency for repeated lookups. Need their QPS profile to estimate.

Ravi Shah: I’ll export QPS per endpoint and sample KV hit rates by EOD. Putting raw CSV in /shared/acme-retail/qps-2026-03-*.csv 

Tom Nguyen: Also pull recent support tickets for Catalog. If they filed integration bugs, that might explain drop.

Aisha Patel: Confirmed — 2 integration tickets last week referencing a failing webhook. I’ll attach the ticket ids in my outreach.

Jen Ortiz: Outreach note draft (quick):
"Victor — seeing a steep drop in Catalog activity and noticed procurement rotated keys last week. Could we hop on a 20-min call to understand if this is a tactical pause for procurement or an evaluation with a competitor? We have two fast fallbacks to keep cold-starts warm and reduce unit costs while you go through procurement. Available today 3-4pm PT or tomorrow morning"

Tom Nguyen: LGTM. Ask for PoC contact + expected duration. If competitor PoC, request the evaluation success metrics so we can map our performance/cost offering.

Aisha Patel: Reaching out now. I’ll post Victor’s reply in this thread.

Lina Morales: If it’s a competitive PoC, I can offer a short demo focused on Catalog retrieval reliability and cost per 1k lookups.

Ravi Shah: For the engineering fallback config, recommend these quick knobs:
- model_variant: redwood-mini-v2
- batch_window_ms: 25
- kv_cache_ttl_secs: 43200

(should be safe to roll to a canary pool)

Tom Nguyen: Great. Assigning action owners: Aisha -> customer outreach; Ravi -> QPS/engineering export + canary config; Lina -> fallback options doc + demo deck; Jen -> renewal playbook readiness. Update here when you have progress.

Aisha Patel: Sent outreach to Victor (cc'd procurement). He replied: "We paused Catalog traffic while procurement finalizes terms; not a technical regression. Procurement is evaluating a vendor pilot that's expected to run for 3 weeks. Would appreciate cost/latency options to present to SRE. — Victor"

Tom Nguyen: Ok pragmatic: not lost yet, but timeboxed PoC. Need a one-pager with cost delta and SLA impact to arm Victor. Lina — can you prioritize the one-pager?

Lina Morales: Will do. Target: 2 slides + 1 cost table by EOD tomorrow.

Ravi Shah: QPS export uploaded. Raw numbers show Catalog median per-minute QPS 120 -> 36 last 14d. KV cache hit rate ~22%.

Jen Ortiz: I’ll update the renewal playbook with this case as "procurement pause — offer fallback + SLAs" so AEs have a quick template.

Tom Nguyen: Thanks team. If anyone finds a hard blocker (billing dispute / security concerns) call it out here immediately. Otherwise we reconvene in this thread once Lina/Ravi have artifacts. :thumbsup:

Aisha Patel: Thanks — will follow up after Lina uploads the one-pager.
